title: senior-by-default config
description: Schema for .claude/do/config.json. `version` is recommended; if omitted, validators MUST default to 1 and emit a warning rather than fail (back-compat). All other fields are optional; defaults documented in config-schema.md. Explicit mismatches (e.g. `version: 2` with this schema) are hard failures. All path-bearing fields resolve relative to the directory containing this config file (not CWD).

^_.description: Underscore-prefixed keys are reserved for human comments (_description, _notes, _setup_notes, etc.) and ignored by validators.

version.description: Schema version. Currently 1. Optional for back-compat: when omitted, validators MUST default to 1 and emit a warning rather than fail. This matches the documented behavior in references/config-validation.md.

commands.description: Per-operation tracker commands. Each command (except close_keyword) accepts either argv array (preferred — argv-safe) or shell string (DEPRECATED — vulnerable to injection through user-controlled {title}/{labels}). See references/trackers.md §Security.

allOf.$comment: Deliberately NO required:['type'] here — this branch must also fire when `type` is omitted: config-schema.md documents github as the default, so an omitted-type config IS a github config and must carry `repo` (every gh invocation in trackers.md passes --repo). Adding required:['type'] would make issue_tracker:{} schema-valid but runtime-broken.

required:['type'] stops this branch firing vacuously when `type` is omitted — pre-fix, {repo:'o/r'} (a documented-valid github-default config) was rejected demanding a custom-tracker `commands` block.

ui_gate.description: null = explicitly disable UI gate; object = enable with given commands.

issue_locale.description: Issue/PR body language: any ISO 639-1 code, optional region (en, ru, ja, ko, pt-BR). Pattern, NOT an enum — Phase 0 auto-init detects ru/ja/ko from $ARGUMENTS, and the pre-fix enum ['ru','en'] made auto-init exit 1 for every Japanese/Korean task.

warn_lines.description: Phase 3.0 WARN threshold on counted lines. LEAVE UNSET unless you mean it: unset, the cap comes from the run's complexity tier (T 50 / L 200 / M 600 / H 1500 — the same buckets plan-size-check gates the plan against), so a WARN means 'this diff exceeded the budget its own plan was approved against'. Setting this pins one flat cap across every tier, which is how the pre-0.13 default (800) ended up below H's own 1500-line plan ceiling and warned on 80% of H runs. Per-run override: --warn-lines.

warn_files.description: Phase 3.0 WARN threshold on counted files. Same tier-derived default as warn_lines (T 2 / L 3 / M 8 / H 25); leave unset to use it. Per-run override: --warn-files.

block_lines.description: Phase 3.0 BLOCK threshold on counted lines (default 2000). Deliberately tier-INDEPENDENT: an unreviewable diff is unreviewable whoever planned it, and it is what lets the PreToolUse hook — which cannot know the run's tier — enforce the same verdict as the gate.

block_files.description: Phase 3.0 BLOCK threshold on counted files (default 50). Tier-independent, same reason as block_lines.

auto_split.description: On a Phase 3.0 BLOCK, split delivery into a stack of sub-cap PRs (Phase 4.2.1) instead of halting. Default true; false reverts to the pre-0.11 draft-PR + blocked hard halt. Per-run override: --no-split.

generated_paths.description: Globs (repo-root-relative) for machine-generated files committed to the repo, e.g. ["openapi/*.json", "**/*.pb.go"]. Their lines/files are excluded from the Phase 3.0 size verdict — a reviewer does not read them line by line; a drift check in CI keeps them correct. Both enforcement tiers read this same key (the pr-size-check wrapper measures, the PreToolUse hook delegates to it), so the gate and the hook cannot disagree. The excluded volume is always printed next to the counted volume. Glob syntax: * (not across /), ** (across /), ? (one non-/ char); a slash-free pattern matches at any depth; a trailing / means everything under. No character classes. Default: [] (nothing excluded).

wip_limit.description: Opt-in. Omit/null disables the Phase 0 Step 1 WIP check entirely.

metrics.description: null = explicit telemetry opt-out (config-ensure-metrics respects it and never re-patches); object = enable. log_path: null keeps the block but disables JSONL emission entirely — the exact opt-out auto-init's _setup_notes advises. Both documented opt-outs were schema-INVALID pre-fix (same nullable shape as ui_gate).

x-allow-extras.description: Fields prefixed with `_` (e.g. `_notes`, `_setup_notes`, `_description`) are reserved for human comments and are tolerated by validators. Strict additionalProperties=false above intentionally rejects unknowns to catch typos; extend the schema rather than add ad-hoc keys.

oneOf.description: PREFERRED: argv array. Each placeholder ({repo}, {title}, {N}, {body_file}, {labels}) occupies a dedicated argv slot — substitution happens after argv split, so user-controlled values cannot smuggle CLI flags.

DEPRECATED string form, accepted ONLY for commands with no user-controlled placeholders. MUST NOT contain `{title}` or `{labels}` — those carry $ARGUMENTS-derived content and are vulnerable to shell injection regardless of `shlex.quote` fallback (the placeholder may already be wrapped in template-side quotes that user content can break out of). Commands carrying user content (typically `create`) MUST use the argv array form.
